skill.name: distributed-debugging-debug-trace
skill.description: Design distributed debugging, tracing, logging, profiling, and production diagnostic workflows for multi-service applications.
skill.summary: Configure practical observability and debugging workflows across development and production systems.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by JavaScript template literals, explicit configuration reads, and ordinary profiler file output. Confirmed risks include unsafe dashboard rendering and debugger exposure. The playbook also contains unauthenticated runtime evaluation and sensitive telemetry patterns that require correction before publication.

remediation.issue: The remote debugger permits unauthenticated runtime expression evaluation and binds debugger interfaces broadly.
remediation.suggestion: Remove remote evaluation or require strong mutual authentication, authorization, TLS, audit logging, strict network isolation, and loopback binding by default.

remediation.issue: Tracing exports complete request bodies and user or session identifiers without redaction.
remediation.suggestion: Replace payload capture with a field allowlist, redact sensitive values, classify telemetry, and enforce access and retention controls.

remediation.issue: The dashboard inserts unauthenticated WebSocket values through innerHTML.
remediation.suggestion: Use authenticated WSS, validate message schemas, and render values with textContent or trusted encoding.

remediation.issue: Production debugging replaces the process-wide console during individual requests.
remediation.suggestion: Use request-scoped logging with asynchronous context and never return unrestricted diagnostic logs to clients.

semantic_findings.title: Unauthenticated Remote Runtime Evaluation
semantic_findings.description: The remote debug server accepts WebSocket messages without authentication and sends caller expressions to Runtime.evaluate. Network clients can execute code in the process.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The server directly routes unauthenticated evaluate messages to the Node.js inspector. The default all-interface binding makes remote access plausible.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Request Data Exported in Traces
semantic_findings.description: The tracing example records complete request bodies, user identifiers, and session identifiers. The configured span processor exports these values to Jaeger.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code explicitly serializes request.body and records user and session identifiers. No field allowlist or redaction occurs before export.

semantic_findings.title: Cross-Request Debug Log Capture
semantic_findings.description: Production middleware replaces the process-wide console during one request. Concurrent request logs can enter another user debug context and expose sensitive data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The console object is global, while capture state belongs to one request. Concurrent application activity can therefore be recorded in the wrong context.

content.value_statement: Distributed failures are difficult to reproduce and correlate across services. This skill designs debugging, tracing, logging, profiling, and production diagnostics workflows.
actual_capabilities: Identifies service boundaries, trace propagation points, and useful spans.
Proposes local and remote debugging configurations for Node.js applications.
Designs OpenTelemetry tracing with Jaeger export and correlation identifiers.
Defines structured logging, sampling, source map, and profiling patterns.
Creates production debugging safeguards using feature flags, tokens, and IP controls.
Provides dashboard, IDE, troubleshooting, and team workflow guidance.
limitations: Examples require adaptation to the application framework, deployment model, and security controls.
The skill does not inspect live systems without access to logs, traces, configuration, or runtime data.
Some playbook examples are unsafe until authentication, redaction, and output encoding are added.
Generated configurations require dependency, performance, and production validation.

use_cases.title: Trace a Microservice Failure
use_cases.description: Map request flow, define spans, and correlate logs for a failure crossing several services.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Debugging
use_cases.description: Create consistent IDE, logging, source map, and profiling practices for a development team.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Production Latency
use_cases.description: Plan sampled tracing and profiling that limits overhead and protects sensitive data.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Local Debugging
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a local debugging setup for [runtime and framework]. Include IDE configuration, source maps, test debugging, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design Distributed Tracing
prompt_templates.prompt: Design tracing for [services and protocols]. Define propagation, key spans, standard attributes, sampling, export, redaction, and coverage tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate observability design for several services.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a Production Incident
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this incident evidence: [logs, traces, symptoms, and timeline]. Correlate signals, rank hypotheses, and propose low-risk diagnostic steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Secure Debugging Platform
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production debugging architecture for [environment]. Include authentication, authorization, encryption, audit logs, data minimization, sampling, retention, and emergency controls.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced platform design with security and governance requirements.

output_examples.input: Requests fail intermittently between the gateway, checkout service, and payment service.
output: Trace plan: propagate one correlation identifier through all three services.
Key spans: gateway validation, checkout orchestration, payment authorization, and dependency calls.
Validation: reproduce one failure and confirm connected spans, error status, and sanitized attributes.

output_examples.input: The Node.js service has rising memory use after each deployment.
output: Baseline: record heap use, allocation rate, request volume, and deployment timestamps.
Profile plan: collect bounded heap snapshots during controlled windows.
Decision path: compare retained object groups before changing application code.

output_examples.input: A team needs production tracing without exposing customer information.
output: Collection policy: allowlist operational attributes and reject request bodies.
Sampling policy: retain errors and rare paths while limiting routine traffic.
Controls: encrypt transport, restrict access, audit queries, and enforce retention.

best_practices: Define a diagnostic question before increasing log detail, trace sampling, or profiler duration.
Allowlist telemetry fields and redact secrets, credentials, tokens, and personal data before export.
Test trace continuity, access controls, overhead, retention, and shutdown behavior before production rollout.
anti_patterns: Do not expose runtime evaluation, inspectors, heap snapshots, or debug routes without strong authentication and network isolation.
Do not record complete request bodies, session identifiers, or arbitrary objects in logs and traces.
Do not use verbose production debugging without sampling, time limits, audit records, and rollback controls.

faq.question: Which systems benefit most from this skill?
faq.answer: Multi-service applications with difficult correlation, intermittent failures, or incomplete observability benefit most.

faq.question: Does the skill require OpenTelemetry?
faq.answer: No. The playbook emphasizes OpenTelemetry, but its workflow can be adapted to other tracing systems.

faq.question: Can it diagnose a live production incident?
faq.answer: It can analyze supplied evidence and propose steps. It needs authorized access and environment details for direct investigation.

faq.question: How should sensitive data be handled?
faq.answer: Use field allowlists, redaction, encryption, restricted access, short retention, and audits for all diagnostic data.

faq.question: Will tracing affect performance?
faq.answer: Tracing adds overhead. Measure baselines, sample traffic, limit attributes, batch exports, and validate under representative load.

faq.question: Are the playbook examples production ready?
faq.answer: No. Adapt and test them, especially remote debugging, telemetry collection, dashboard rendering, authentication, and error handling.
